clue.text: Bury division: agreement's charter for resolution

indicators.note: a resolution is a working-out or rearranging, so these letters are to be resolved into a new order

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter of the pool
taken as written

explanation.surface: A council wrangle in the town of Bury, where a signed agreement is meant to settle a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for resolution' rearranges all of AGREEMENTS and CHARTER. Bury is a town in north-west England, one of the boroughs that make up this metropolitan county.
explanation.definitionFit: Bury is one of the borough divisions of this English metropolitan county, so the county is what Bury is a division of.

clue.text: Hit target? Try one that got to No 10 in the sixties

parts.note: to have a go is to try

parts.words: one that got to No 10 in the sixties
parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home became Prime Minister, living at No 10 Downing Street, in 1963

explanation.surface: Sounds like a question about a darts throw and a hit record reaching number ten in the sixties chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' is not a chart position but 10 Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike home is to hit the target, and the two-word phrase is used the same way of a shot or remark landing.

clue.text: Daft turning up around end of Beggar's Opera

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the letter, enclosing it
in a down answer, turning up reads the word for daft from bottom to top

parts.note: daft means inane

indicators.note: the last letter of the word Beggar's is taken

explanation.surface: Someone foolish is getting excited about John Gay's Beggar's Opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses INANE to ENANI; 'around' puts it round R, from 'end of Beggar's'. The Beggar's Opera is a famous English ballad opera, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's early opera based on Victor Hugo's play Hernani is a single example of the genre named in the clue.

clue.text: Prescriptions for Verity coming from Yanks — pity doctor's got involved

indicators.note: the pity and doctor pieces get involved in, that is placed inside, the word for yanks

parts.note: yanks as a verb means tugs
ruth is an old word for pity, as in ruthless
DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Americans bring medicines for a woman named Verity, and an involved doctor is pitied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got involved' is the container signal. Verity, read as a woman's name, is really the word for truth, so the drugs given to extract it are cryptically its prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium pentothal and similar serums are given to extract honesty, so they are cryptically remedies prescribed for verity.

clue.text: In Edinburgh, busy on public transport

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A note that in Edinburgh the buses are crowded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' is British slang for a police officer or detective. Ian Rankin's Inspector Rebus is a fictional detective working in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Rebus is the fictional detective of Ian Rankin's novels, a policeman, or busy in slang, based in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Loud telling-off makes one wary

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
an earful is a scolding or telling-off

explanation.surface: Being shouted at makes someone cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary is apprehensive of danger, and fearful likewise means anxious or afraid of what may happen.

clue.text: Historian's succinct description of snooker player's strength?

definitions.meaning: Sir John ... wrote the multi-volume history of the British Army

definitions.text: succinct description of snooker player's strength?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., it says in three words that his strong point is his cue

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how briefly to sum up what a snooker player is best at.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Historian's means 'is'. The second half reads as a short phrase: his forte is his cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortescue is the surname of Sir John Fortescue, the military historian, so it names a historian.

clue.text: Agreed to hug children in pain

indicators.note: the word for agreed hugs, that is encloses, the abbreviation

parts.note: ay is a word of agreement, a yes

explanation.surface: Someone consents to embrace hurting children.
explanation.definitionFit: Achy describes someone suffering dull aches, so it means hurting or in pain.

clue.text: Make a brass knocker? That?s nothing, really

parts.note: to forge is to make, especially in metal
knocker is slang for a breast, and tit is a cheap or brassy synonym

explanation.surface: Someone asks about making a metal door knocker and is told not to bother.
explanation.walkthrough: The door-knocker picture misleads: the knocker here is the vulgar slang one. The phrase 'That's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it was nothing, really, dismisses thanks or a matter, just as the idiom telling someone not to think more about it does.

clue.text: Man in suit, some distance from China, chasing game soldier perhaps

parts.note: the li is a Chinese unit of distance
tig is the playground chasing game also called tag
a soldier is one caste of ant, so ant is given by example

explanation.surface: A man, a long way from China, follows a game soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing; 'chasing' only links, and suits the game of tig, which is all about chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A party bringing or defending a lawsuit is a person involved in a suit at law.

clue.text: Believer showing rear for all to see

parts.note: hind means rear, as in hind legs
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Someone displaying their backside to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Hindu religion is an adherent of a faith, so a believer.

clue.text: Actress's long, central part on radio

indicators.note: broadcast on radio, the words are only heard, so their sound counts

parts.note: to burn is to long, and the heart is the central part

explanation.surface: An actress has a long central role in a radio play.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN (long) and HEART (central part) said together give the surname. Sarah Bernhardt was the celebrated French stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Bernhardt was the most famous French stage performer of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: See 1
Composer's second-rate bit of work

parts.note: B is the second grade, so second-rate
the erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is judged mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Composer's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, writer of Wozzeck.

clue.text: Gilt attire might become them

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase might become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Gold-trimmed clothing would suit celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might become' rearranges GILT ATTIRE, and also says such clothes might suit them, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable celebrities wearing gold-spangled outfits fit the picture of glamorous people whom gilded clothing suits.

clue.text: Rogue performances by Public Enemy Number One returning on visit

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece being on another means it comes after it

parts.note: Public Enemy is an American hip-hop group, so their performances are raps
to call is to pay a visit

indicators.note: the abbreviation pair for Number One is read backwards

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number, and I is one

explanation.surface: A villain, Public Enemy Number One, comes back on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NO I round to make ION; 'on' places it after the visit word. 'Public Enemy Number One' looks like one phrase but splits into the band and the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or scoundrel is a rogue, an old-fashioned word for a mischievous person.

clue.text: China unclear about role initially, reading between the lines?

parts.note: china, from rhyming slang china plate, means mate or pal

indicators.note: the word for unclear goes about the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: misty means hazy or unclear

indicators.note: the first letter of the word role is taken

explanation.surface: A vague remark about the role of China in some diplomatic reading of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from 'role'; 'about' puts MISTY round it. China is cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm reading interprets the lines on the hand, so it is literally reading the lines, cryptically between them.

clue.text: H-Hook-like?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Captain Hook of Peter Pan is a pirate

explanation.surface: A stuttering comparison to something hook-shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: Hook-like means like Hook, so AS comes first. The repeated H mimics a stammer but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H stands for the breathy sound phoneticians name with this word, which also means to pronounce it.

clue.text: Cure mild hiccups, bringing instrument

indicators.note: hiccups are disruptions, so the letters of the phrase are disrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A remedy for a slight bout of hiccups that involves a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiccups' rearranges CURE MILD.
explanation.definitionFit: The dulcimer is a stringed musical instrument played by striking with small hammers.

clue.text: Hack GQ utilises good for the most slovenly of writing

indicators.note: to hack is to chop up roughly, so the letters are hacked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hack writer at the magazine GQ produces the sloppiest prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' rearranges GQ UTILISES with G for good. A hack writer is the misleading sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting full of scrawly lines is untidy, so the most scrawled is the most slovenly writing.

clue.text: Friend of Sartre entertaining Jarry briefly in Italian resort

indicators.note: the word for friend entertains, that is holds inside, the short name

parts.note: ami is French for friend, as Sartre the French philosopher would say

indicators.note: a first name given briefly is cut to its short familiar form

parts.note: Alfred Jarry was the French playwright of Ubu Roi

explanation.surface: Sartre's friend hosts the playwright Jarry on the Italian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts ALFRED to ALF; 'entertaining' sets that inside AMI. The French setting of Sartre and Jarry fits the friend being French.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a town on the Amalfi Coast of southern Italy, a well-known holiday destination.

clue.text: Partners for singles to boot solitude — finally — out

indicators.note: the chosen letter is put out of the longer word

parts.note: to boot means in addition, besides

indicators.note: the last letter of the word solitude is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to single people to kick out loneliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'solitude'; 'out' drops it from BESIDES. 'Singles' are records, not unattached people.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vinyl single record, the flip side carries the secondary track, so these are the hit's companions.

clue.text: Heads off in total chaos: hundreds are dying

indicators.note: read as heads of, the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Total disorder as heads roll and hundreds perish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' takes the first letters of In Total Chaos Hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dying to do something is to long eagerly for it, and this verb in the plural means the same craving.

clue.text: Winner alongside podium that is covered in common flowers

indicators.note: the first name sits alongside the next piece, before it

parts.note: Michael Winner was a British film director, so his first name is Michael

indicators.note: the podium and abbreviation pieces are covered in, enclosed by, the word for common

parts.note: mass, as in mass appeal, means common or popular
a dais is a raised podium
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A race winner stands beside the podium decked in ordinary flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' is the container signal; 'alongside' just puts the name first. Michael Winner was a British film director, so 'Winner' gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: These are autumn-flowering asters, blooming around the feast of St Michael in late September.

clue.text: Demanding to keep ecstasy, did speed

indicators.note: the word for demanding keeps, that is holds, the letter inside

parts.note: a demanding task is hard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone insisting on keeping their ecstasy pills went fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush off at great speed, like a hare, is to have run fast, so the past tense matches did speed.

clue.text: Withdrawal from bank, Hatton Cross

indicators.note: the letters are withdrawn from within the words, taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A cash withdrawal from a bank near Hatton Cross, a London Underground station by Heathrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawal from' takes the letters from inside 'bank, Hatton'. Hatton Cross is a Tube station near Heathrow Airport, which makes 'Cross' look part of a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the looped cross of ancient Egypt, a symbol of life.

clue.text: Carpeting from a cross vicar I ignored once

parts.note: X is a cross

indicators.note: one of the two letters is ignored, left out just once

parts.note: a vicar is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A carpet comes from a bad-tempered vicar whom someone once ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored once' drops one I from MINISTER. 'cross' looks like angry but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Troubled when TV cook returns

indicators.note: the name is read backwards, returning to where it began

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook

explanation.surface: Someone is worried at a television chef's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses DELIA. Delia Smith is a long-standing British TV cookery presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been unwell or in difficulty is to have been troubled, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Coarse stocking line — out of this world!

indicators.note: the word for coarse is stocking, holding inside it, the letter

parts.note: earthy humour is coarse or crude

explanation.surface: Rough hosiery with a ladder is declared fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' normally means superb; read literally, as coming out of this world, it means worldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes from this world rather than heaven is mundane and terrestrial, so worldly.
